title: Projectivity over a complete Noetherian base from a projective reduction
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring that is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], let $A\to B$ be of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $M$ be a finite $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Assume $M/IM$ is projective over $A/I$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, regard $M\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ as a $B$-module by the canonical action [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Assume that for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$ which is an associated prime of this $B$-module (the annihilator of an element, as in [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]), one has $IB+\mathfrak q\ne B$. Then $M$ is projective over $A$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], the Noetherianity of $A$ and finite type of $A\to B$ imply that $B$ is Noetherian. Define $\widehat M=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}M/I^nM$ as the module of compatible residue classes, and let $u:M\to\widehat M$ send $m$ to $(m\bmod I^nM)_n$. These are exactly the completion and canonical map used below.

source.place: Tag 05DP, first sentence of proof, with the preceding remark before Tag 05DL and Algebra Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-completion-universally-injective] with $(R,S,P)=(A,B,M)$. Both rings are Noetherian by the hypotheses and step 1; $M$ is finite over $B$ and flat over $A$ by assumption. The prime condition is exactly the assumption on associated primes of the $B$-modules $M\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, with $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$. Hence $u\otimes_A1_Q$ is injective for every $A$-module $Q$.

source.place: Tag 05DP, first sentence of proof, invoking Tag 05DM (lemma-universally-injective-to-completion-flat).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-completion-flat-mittag-leffler] with $(R,I,P)=(A,I,M)$. Its hypotheses are precisely Noetherianity and completeness of $A$, flatness of $M$ over $A$, and projectivity of $M/IM$ over $A/I$. It follows that $\widehat M$ is a Mittag-Leffler $A$-module (and flat). No finiteness of $M$ over $A$ is required.

source.place: Tag 05DP, second sentence of proof, invoking Tag 05DK (lemma-lift-ML).

proof.text: Here is the short tensor argument behind the pure-submodule clause of Algebra Tag 059N. Fix any family $(Q_j)_{j\in J}$ of $A$-modules. For $x\in M\otimes_A\prod_j Q_j$ with $\theta_{M,(Q_j)}(x)=0$, naturality gives $\theta_{\widehat M,(Q_j)}((u\otimes1)(x))=(\prod_j(u\otimes1_{Q_j}))(\theta_{M,(Q_j)}(x))=0$. This identity holds on $m\otimes(q_j)_j$, where both sides are $(u(m)\otimes q_j)_j$, hence on every tensor. By step 3 and [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module], $\theta_{\widehat M,(Q_j)}$ is injective, so $(u\otimes1)(x)=0$. Step 2 applied to $Q=\prod_jQ_j$ gives $x=0$. Thus $M$ is Mittag-Leffler by the same definition.

source.place: Tag 059N, lemma-pure-submodule-ML (1), its tensor diagram, expanded directly from the tensor criterion of Tag 059M.

proof.text: Choose algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $B$ over $A$ by [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and module generators $m_1,\ldots,m_r$ of $M$ over $B$ by [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The elements $b_1^{e_1}\cdots b_d^{e_d}m_j$ with $(e_1,\ldots,e_d)\in\mathbf N^d$ and $1\le j\le r$ generate $M$ over $A$: write $m=\sum_j c_jm_j$ and expand each $c_j$ as a finite polynomial in the $b_i$. This set is countable, since for each total degree there are finitely many exponent tuples, and it is a countable union over the degrees. When $d=0$, the sole empty monomial is $1$; when $r=0$, $M=0$ and the generating set is empty.

source.place: Tag 05DP, final sentence: the assertion that N is countably generated, expanded using finite type and finite generation.

proof.text: The $A$-module $M$ is flat by assumption, Mittag-Leffler by step 4, and countably generated by step 5. Therefore [lem-trf-countable-flat-mittag-leffler-projective], applied with $R=A$ and $P=M$, proves that $M$ is projective over $A$.

source.place: Tag 05DP, final sentence, invoking Algebra Tag 059X (lemma-countgen-projective).
